text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The caretaker government has prepared a draft law on "Freedom of Information" suggesting ban on the disclosure of record concerning superior courts, armed forces, financial institutions, intelligence agencies and ministries like defence, foreign affairs and cabinet.
- Caretaker chief minister of Sindh province Mumtaz Bhutto has agreed to pay 1.0 billion rupees as golden handshake to 3,300 employees of the Karachi Transport Corporation.
- An important Republican congressman, who is a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has urged the U.S. government to publicly support the holding of February 3 elections in Pakistan.

- The Clinton Administration has decided to give incentives to Pakistan and India to give up their nuclear options as sanctions on arms purchases and economic aid have failed to pressure any one of them.
- Pakistan Muslim League President Nawaz Sharif has said those who have boycotted the elections or were pursuading others to stay away from the electoral process would get nothing.

- Addressing election rallies in Karachi, deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto said the verdict in favour of her Pakistan People's Party in February 3 elections would amount to rejection of presidential form of government.
- The interim government has finanlised a new textile quota policy aimed at discouraging the under-utilisation of quota, ensuring value addition and facilitating new exporters.

- Massive withdrawal of foreign investment from the local bourse, liquidity crunch and economic instability slashed the profits of seven brokerage houses listed at the Karachi Stock Exchange by 46.5 percent to 50.31 million rupees as against 108.18 million in 1995.

- A drastic drop of 54.53 percent has been noticed in the import of powdered milk during the first half of 1996/97 because of increased fresh milk production in the country, high taxes and other cost push measures.
- The sales of local beverage industry dropped by 25 percent in 1996 due to heavy taxation, affecting government revenues which also declined by 14.5 percent.
- The Internationl Monetary Fund has further delayed the second tranche of $53 million standby loan to Pakistan.
- The Instaphone cellular phone company has withdrawn its compensation claim against the government and requested restoration of its phone service in Karachi.
